findings.issue: The slot `distributions` is not present in the supplied schema digest for the Dataset/CoreDataset slot inventory. The digest declares `file_collections` (range FileCollection) for grouping files, and `distribution_formats` (range DistributionFormat) for formats. Neither `distributions` nor its child keys `path`, `md5`, `bytes`, or a scalar `conforms_to_standard: RO_CRATE` on a distribution object are attested by the digest. If the core schema does not declare this slot, the ten distribution objects will fail validation and the entire per-file inventory is lost.

Content stated in the core record that the full record does not state in the same form: the ten per-file MD5 checksums, file paths, and media types appear in the core record under `distributions` with a dedicated `md5` key, whereas the full record carries the same checksums only as prose inside `file_collections[].description`. The core record must not assert structured content absent from the full record; either the full record needs the equivalent structure or the core must degrade to the full record's representation.

Each FileCollection object embeds file size, MD5 checksum, and publication date as prose inside `description` while leaving the declared structured keys `file_count` and `total_bytes` unpopulated. The digest declares `total_bytes` as integer and `file_count` as integer on FileCollection; the Dataverse table gives only rounded display sizes ("3.8 GB", "113.3 KB"), so `total_bytes` is legitimately unpopulatable, but the checksum has no declared home on FileCollection and its placement in prose is the only available option. Flagged as a representation weakness rather than an unsupported claim.

Value 10 is asserted as the total number of files across all file collections. The bundle's June 2026 Dataverse file table lists 10 distributed archive files, which supports the count of top-level archives; however the schema describes this slot as aggregated from file_collections[].file_count, and no `file_count` is populated on any FileCollection, so the aggregate is not internally derivable. The value is bundle-supported at the archive level but inconsistent with the slot's stated aggregation basis.

`mailto:ravitskyv@thehastingscenter.org` is used as the identifier for a Person. The digest declares `id` as `uriorcurie`. A mailto URI is a syntactically valid URI, but the v5 identifier rule states a person is identified by a personal-identifier registry entry; the bundle supplies ORCID:0000-0002-7080-8801 for Vardit Ravitsky in the same June 2026 release author metadata, which is the attested personal identifier and should be preferred over the contact email.

`mailto:jean-christophe_belisle-pipon@sfu.ca` is used as the Person identifier. The bundle supplies ORCID:0000-0002-8965-8153 for Jean-Christophe Bélisle-Pipon in the same June 2026 release author metadata; the attested ORCID should be preferred over a mailto URI for a person identifier.

`mailto:jillianparker@health.ucsd.edu` is used as the Person identifier for Jillian Parker. The bundle supplies ORCID:0000-0003-4535-3486 for Parker J in the June 2026 release author metadata; the attested personal registry identifier should be preferred over a mailto URI.

`https://reporter.nih.gov/project-details/11211616` is a resolver URL used as a Grant identifier in a `uriorcurie`-ranged slot. No schema-declared prefix for NIH RePORTER applications is evident in the digest, so a URL is the permitted fallback; however the bundle also supplies the bare award numbers 1OT2OD032742-01, 3OT2OD032742-01S2, and core project OT2OD032742, and the chosen URL is the source page rather than the grant identifier itself. Flagged for review of whether the grant identifier or the source URL was intended.

FundingMechanism object populates only `grantor` with the composite string 'University of Virginia, Frederick Thomas Fund'. This conflates the institution and the named fund into a single grantor value. The bundle states 'the Frederick Thomas Fund of the University of Virginia' in the project descriptor acknowledgements; the value is bundle-supported in substance but packs two entities into one field where the class offers `grants` for the specific instrument.

B2AI_SUBSTRATE:59 is 'Size Exclusion Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry Data', which fits the SEC-MS elution profile instance. Correct. Recorded only to note that the neighbouring AP-MS instance uses B2AI_SUBSTRATE:58 'Mass Spectrometry Data', which is the correct general term since no AP-MS-specific substrate exists. No defect.

B2AI_TOPIC:19 is 'Microscale Imaging'. The immunofluorescence confocal images of subcellular protein localization are plausibly covered, but B2AI_TOPIC:15 'Image' is the more direct term and the vocabulary offers no 'spatial proteomics' or 'subcellular imaging' entry. The chosen term is defensible; flagged as a judgment call rather than an error.

B2AI_SUBSTRATE:64 'Perturb-seq Data' is used for the single-cell CRISPR interference transcriptional profile instance. This is the correct and most specific term. No defect. Recorded to contrast with instances[4], which uses B2AI_SUBSTRATE:63 'Single-cell RNA Sequence Data' for the raw reads — also defensible, though the raw sequence instance is itself perturb-seq data and the two substrate assignments draw a distinction the bundle does not explicitly make.

Four Creator objects are asserted, each populating only `principal_investigator`. Three of the four (Krogan, Lundberg, Ideker) carry the institutional affiliation as prose inside the nested Person `description` rather than in the Creator-level `affiliations` slot, which the digest declares as Organization[]. Only the Clark entry populates `affiliations`, and it does so because the bundle supplies a ROR for UVA. The asymmetry is defensible under the identifier rule (no ROR attested for UCSD, UCSF, Stanford) but means three of four Creator objects leave a declared structural slot empty while restating its content in free text — the v3 rule against prose-in-description where a declared field exists.

The Creator class as digested exposes `principal_investigator` (Person), `affiliations`, and `credit_roles`. All four entries characterize the person's contribution in prose inside `description` (e.g. 'The size-exclusion chromatography mass spectrometry ... datasets in this release were generated in the Krogan laboratory') while `credit_roles` — which offers `data_curation`, `investigation`, `resources`, `supervision`, `project_administration`, `software`, `methodology` — is left empty throughout. The bundle's contribution statement in the Nature methods and the CM4AI module descriptions support role assignment for at least Ideker (supervision, project_administration) and Clark (data_curation, software).

The release citation names 47 authors; four Creator objects are emitted. The source_caveats explain this as a scoping decision forced by the Creator class exposing only `principal_investigator`. This is a defensible reading, but it means the record omits 43 attested creators, and the four retained are presented under a slot whose Person sub-slot asserts principal-investigator status for Timothy Clark, whom the bundle describes as lead author of the project descriptor and Standards module lead rather than as a project PI. The NIH RePORTER record names IDEKER, TREY as the sole principal investigator.

'The Hastings Center' is asserted as the reviewing organization for Vardit Ravitsky, inferred from the mailto domain thehastingscenter.org in the release ethics contact block. The bundle's June 2026 release author metadata records 'Ravitsky V, University of Montreal'. The record's own source_caveats acknowledge this conflict and correctly note both statements sit in the same tier-1 source so ranking cannot decide — yet the slot nonetheless selects one value rather than representing the disagreement. Under the uniform rule for same-tier disagreement, the value should represent what the evidence states rather than silently selecting.

Both EthicalReview objects describe named individual ethics contacts and the project's ethics-guideline work, but neither records an IRB approval, ethics committee determination, or compliance certification — which is what the slot description asks for. The bundle states the dataset involves no human subjects, so no IRB review exists to record; the objects therefore populate the slot with governance-contact information in place of the review facts the slot exists to carry. Arguably the slot should be omitted and this content carried under data_governance.stewardship_roles, where it is already partly duplicated.

The digest does not show `regulatory_compliance` as a list-ranged slot on HumanSubjectResearch, and the value here is a single-element list containing a long prose paragraph. If the slot is scalar, the list wrapper is a shape error; if multivalued, packing three distinct compliance facts (no human subjects, de-identified samples, not FDA regulated, plus the HipSci MTA condition) into one string collapses entities the slot would separate.

Single-element list restating the three governance booleans already asserted structurally in `human_subject_research.involves_human_subjects` (false) and `is_deidentified.identifiable_elements_present` (false). Duplicative rather than unsupported; the ExportControlRegulatoryRestrictions class also offers `confidentiality_level` and `hipaa_compliant`, and the bundle's 'Human Subjects: No / De-identified: Yes / FDA Regulated: No' block supports `hipaa_compliant: not_applicable`, which is left unpopulated.

Value 'CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0'. The bundle states the license as 'CC BY-NC-SA 4.0' throughout the Dataverse records and links https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/. The hyphenated form is a reasonable SPDX-style normalization (SPDX identifier is CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0) but is not the string any source uses. Low-risk normalization, flagged for consistency review.

`ROR:0153tk833` is asserted as the publisher. The bundle attests this ROR only as an author affiliation identifier attached to five UVA-affiliated authors in the June 2026 release metadata; it does not state that ROR:0153tk833 is the publisher of the dataset. The Dataverse breadcrumb identifies the publisher as 'University of Virginia Dataverse'. Using an affiliation ROR as a publisher identifier is an inference the bundle supports only weakly — though the institution is the same and the identifier is attested in-bundle.
'2026-06-17T00:00:00Z' matches the release publication date. Correct RFC 3339 form with UTC offset. No defect.

'2026-07-15T00:00:00Z' is taken from the three immunofluorescence archive file publication dates, while the dataset-level publication date is 2026-06-17. The record's source_caveats explain this choice. Defensible, but the Dataverse page for the June 2026 release does not state a dataset-level last-modified date, so this is a derived value rather than an attested one.

'2025-02-27T00:00:00Z' is taken from the Dataverse 'Data Creation Date' and 'Deposit Date' fields, both 2025-02-27. These fields are inherited unchanged across the March 2025, June 2025, October 2025, and June 2026 release records, so the value describes the release series rather than this specific release's creation. Bundle-supported but of limited meaning for the June 2026 referent.

`RO_CRATE` is asserted at dataset level. The June 2026 release distributes `cm4ai_release_metadata.zip` containing RO-Crate metadata, and the project descriptor states outputs are packaged as RO-Crates. Supported. However the same digest's `conforms_to` prose additionally mentions the EVI Evidence Graph Ontology, Schema.org, and the ARK identifier scheme, none of which map to a declared enum value, and `OTHER` is not additionally emitted. Minor under-specification rather than an error.

The full 47-author citation string is carried in `notes` on the core record because the core schema lacks a `citation` slot. The digest's guidance for `notes` is 'residual content only, after every fitting slot is used ... never invent keys'. Relocating a citation into notes is a reasonable fallback, but it means the core record's notes assert content (the complete author list) that appears in the full record under `citation` — a slot-level divergence between the paired records that the reconciliation should have surfaced as a projection loss rather than a silent relocation.

Both Subpopulation objects describe cell lines rather than demographic or other subgroups of instances within the dataset. The digest describes this slot as covering 'demographic or other groups, their representation, and any imbalances'. Cell-line strata are a defensible reading of 'other groups', and the donor demographics (51-year-old Black female; healthy male Northern European) are attested, but the objects are functionally dataset subsets and might belong in `subsets` (DataSubset) instead — which is left empty in both records.

Omitted despite clear bundle support. The June 2026 release distributes data partitioned along two crossed axes the bundle states explicitly: cell line (MDA-MB-468, KOLF2.1J and its NPC/neuron/cardiomyocyte derivatives) and treatment condition (untreated, paclitaxel, vorinostat). These are logical partitions of the dataset and DataSubset requires only `id`. The imaging archives in particular are distributed as three condition-specific subsets.

Omitted. Correct — the bundle contains no statement of offensive, disturbing, or harmful content, and the data are laboratory measurements from cell lines. Recorded to confirm the omission is evidence-grounded rather than an oversight.

Omitted. Correct — the bundle states no human subjects were involved and data derive from commercially available de-identified cell lines, so no participant consent was obtained or documented. Omission is the right answer.

Omitted despite partial bundle support. The June 2026 release states 'Some datasets are under temporary pre-publication embargo' and marks both perturb-seq external datasets as Embargoed. Embargo is a restriction on release that Confidentiality (with `confidential_elements_present` and `confidentiality_details`) could carry. The fact is recorded in `missing_data_documentation` and `regulatory_restrictions.other_compliance` instead, so it is not lost, but the more fitting slot is empty.

Omitted. The bundle records one correction event (the June 2025 revision adding RGB images and correcting RO-Crate metadata), which is captured under `errata`. No data-quality anomaly is described in the bundle. Omission correct.

Omitted. The bundle's Nature methods describe extensive quality-control and filtering for the U2OS study, but that is a different dataset. For the CM4AI cell-line release the bundle states only that perturb-seq 'resulting data are currently being QCed' (project descriptor, tier 3, describing Year 1 status). This is too thin and too dated to support a CleaningStrategy object for the June 2026 release. Omission defensible.

Omitted despite bundle support for the imaging modality. The bundle states antibody quality was scored according to a standard HPA protocol with the highest-scoring antibody per protein selected, and that images carry four defined channels with specified reference markers. The Nature source additionally describes an Annotation Jamboree curation process — but that pertains to the U2OS map, not this release. The HPA antibody-selection detail is the CM4AI-relevant part and could support a LabelingStrategy object.

Omitted. Correct — the bundle describes no train/validation/test partitioning of the CM4AI cell-line data. The FileCollection `collection_type` enum offers training_split/test_split/validation_split, and none is used, consistent with the absence of splits.

Omitted. The bundle describes protein-protein interaction networks as a central data product — AP-MS interaction edges and SEC-MS co-elution similarity between protein pairs are literally relationships between instances. The Relationships class (`relationship_details`) is the declared home for 'how instances relate (e.g. graph edges ... )'. The interaction structure is described in prose in the dataset description and instances but not in the slot that exists for it.

Omitted. Defensible — the release distributes image archives and packaged mass-spectrometry and perturb-seq products rather than a tabular file with described columns, and `is_tabular` is correctly false. The bundle supplies no variable-level dictionary for the distributed files.

Omitted. Correct for this release — no inter-annotator agreement statistics are reported for the CM4AI cell-line data. The Nature source reports GPT-4 naming reproducibility and confidence scores, but those concern the U2OS map annotation, a different dataset explicitly excluded from this record's referent.

Omitted despite arguable support. The project descriptor states the MuSIC pipeline uses a large language model approach to name protein assemblies and assign a name confidence score, and uses node2vec and a HPA DenseNet-derived model for embeddings. These are automated annotation tools used in the project's dataset creation. However, computed cell maps are excluded from this release, so the tools did not produce anything distributed here — omission is defensible on referent grounds.
Omitted. Correct — the bundle states missing components are documented rather than imputed, which the record captures in `missing_data_documentation.handling_strategy`. No imputation is described.
Omitted. Correct — no individuals were notified because no individuals were the subject of collection; the bundle states no human subjects.
Omitted. Correct — no consent was obtained, so no revocation mechanism exists or is described.
Omitted. Correct — the bundle describes no DPIA. The ethics work described is value-repository and guideline development, not privacy impact assessment.
Omitted. Correct — no human subjects, therefore no at-risk population protections to record.
Omitted. Correct and consistent with the human_subject_research assertion.
Omitted. Correct — no participants.
Omitted. Correct — the de-identification status is carried in `is_deidentified`, which is the fitting slot for cell-line-derived data with no participants.

Omitted despite partial support. The project descriptor states the Cell Mapping Toolkit is distributed on GitHub (https://github.com/idekerlab/cellmaps_pipeline) with a step-by-step guide, and describes the toolkit as 'a flexible and generalizable framework ... enabling researchers to integrate and construct cell maps via multiple input modalities'. This concerns extending the software rather than contributing to the dataset, so the omission is defensible, but the ExtensionMechanism `contribution_url` has a plausible candidate.
Omitted. Correct — the bundle names no citation index or use-tracking registry for this dataset. The Dataverse page explicitly states 'Sorry, no citations were found.'

Omitted. The bundle's intended-use list is captured under `intended_uses` and `tasks`, and no source describes applications beyond the creators' original intent. Defensible omission, though the Nature source's use cases (structural modelling seeding, cell-type-specificity analysis, tumour mutation interpretation) suggest analogous downstream tasks — those belong to the U2OS dataset and are correctly excluded from this referent.

Omitted. The June 2026 release is one in a quarterly series, all of which are recorded under `related_datasets` with relationship_type `is_new_version_of`. No source states a hasPart/isPartOf hierarchy, so omission is correct; recorded to confirm the series relationship was placed in the fitting slot rather than misfiled here.

Omitted from both records; the full record uses `file_collections` for the ten archives, which the digest identifies as the correct slot for file groupings ('For file collections, use the file_collections attribute instead'). Correct choice.

Omitted. The digest declares this as a string slot for a resource from which this resource was derived. The bundle attests that the distributed data products derive from raw instrument data deposited in MassIVE and the SRA, which the record captures under `raw_data_sources`. Since no single scalar source predominates and the raw sources are already structurally recorded, omission is defensible.

Omitted while `creators` is populated. Defensible — the digest describes `created_by` as 'the person or organization primarily responsible', and the release names Trey Ideker as point of contact and UCSD as the awardee organization. A value is available if the slot is wanted; its absence is not a factual defect.

Omitted. The bundle names Justin Niestroy as the Dataverse depositor, which the record carries in `maintainers[1].maintainer_details` as prose. Depositor is not clearly 'contributed to modifying or updating', so the omission is defensible, though the fact is present in the record only as free text.

Omitted from the full record (and the core schema has no counterpart). Defensible given only rounded display sizes are available, and the record's source_caveats state this explicitly for the core distributions. Recorded to confirm the omission is reasoned. Note the project portal states a project-wide 21.4 TB figure, correctly excluded here as an aggregate over all releases rather than this one.

The description asserts 'Ten archive files are distributed, of which the three immunofluorescence image archives account for approximately 12.6 GB of the release volume'. The 12.6 GB figure is a computed sum (3.8 + 4.6 + 4.2) of rounded display sizes, not a value any source states. Arithmetic on source-stated roundings produces a derived quantity presented as fact; it should be attributed as approximate-derived or omitted.

The description states MDA-MB-468 donor as 'a 51-year-old Black female'. The project descriptor's wording is 'a 51-year-old black female'. Capitalization is an editorial normalization consistent with the American-English style instruction and does not alter the claim. No defect.

The description states RRID:CVCL_0419 for MDA-MB-468 and RRID:CVCL_B5P3 for KOLF2.1J. Both are attested verbatim in the project descriptor preprint (tier 3). Correctly sourced. Recorded to note these are the only cell-line registry identifiers in the record and they appear only in prose, not in any identifier-ranged slot — which is appropriate, since no slot exists for cell-line RRIDs.

States 'multimodal interrogation of 100 chromatin modifiers and 100 metabolic enzymes'. This figure comes from the bioRxiv project descriptor (tier 3), which describes the project's stated objective. The tier-1 June 2026 release does not restate these panel sizes, and the tier-2 cm4ai.org data-releases page gives different flagship figures (523 proteins with IF images, 200 genes perturb-seq for TNBC). The record's source_caveats address the IF protein-count conflict but not the panel-size figures, which may be similarly superseded.

The single CollectionTimeframe populates only `timeframe_details` and `source_caveats`, leaving the declared `start_date` and `end_date` (both range date) empty. The bundle supplies 2025-02-27 as the data creation date, which could populate `start_date`. The prose correctly notes collection is ongoing, so `end_date` is properly absent, but the available start date is stated in prose rather than in its declared field — the v3 prose-in-description pattern.

The record's own source_caveats state 'the release citation lists 47 named authors'. Counting the author list in the June 2026 citation yields 47 names. Verified consistent. However the same caveat block in the full record says 'reproduced in full in the citation slot' while the core record's equivalent caveat drops that clause and the citation lives in `notes` — a small internal divergence between the paired caveat texts that reflects the unresolved projection issue flagged above.
Full record declares `Dataset`, core declares `CoreDataset`. Correct per the digest, which specifies Dataset for a full datasheet and CoreDataset for a core one. No defect.

'10.18130/V3/HIGT4C' is the bare DOI, correctly excluding the doi: CURIE prefix and the resolver URL, per the slot description and the v5 rule that the string-ranged doi slot takes the bare form. Correct.

`doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C` uses the doi: CURIE form in the uriorcurie-ranged id slot, correctly per the v5 rule. The same CURIE form is used consistently for related_datasets targets and version_access.latest_version_doi. Internally consistent and rule-compliant.

Sub-part identifiers are minted as fragments on the dataset DOI CURIE (e.g. doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C#apms-mda-mb-468-paclitaxel). This follows the v5 minting rule — fragment on an attested identifier for a label with no referent outside the record. Correct approach. Note however that a fragment appended to a DOI CURIE is not a standard resolvable form; the rule permits it as the best available option and no better anchor exists.

One DatasetBias object with `bias_type: representation_bias`. The bundle's stated bias — 'derived from commercially available de-identified human cell lines ... does not represent all biological variants which may be seen in the population at large' — maps well to representation_bias. However `mitigation_strategy` is left empty and the bundle offers none, and the `affected_subsets` value is prose describing the whole dataset rather than naming subsets. Minor shape weakness.

`access_review_process` states that files are openly downloadable without an access request AND that a Data Access Committee supervises distribution. These come from different tiers (Dataverse file table, tier 1; project descriptor, tier 3) and describe different regimes. The value presents both without flagging the tension. The committee's actual role appears to be commercial dual-licensing rather than gating open access, which the text partly conveys but does not clearly separate.

Omitted despite the class declaring it (range Organization). The bundle attests UCSD as awardee and the Regents of the University of California as copyright holder. An Organization object without a registry identifier could still carry a name. Minor structural gap; the information is present in `ip_restrictions` and `maintainers` as prose.

Omitted despite the class declaring it. The bundle names Jillian Parker as the Data Governance Committee contact and Trey Ideker as the dataset point of contact; either would be a defensible licensing contact. Not a factual error, but a declared field left empty where a candidate exists.
'Quarterly' matches the release statement and the portal FAQ ('CM4AI releases data quarterly'). Consistent across tier 1 and tier 2. Correct.

'2.0' is asserted for the June 2026 release, matching the Dataverse 'Version 2.0' header. Correct. Note the internal inconsistency in the source itself: the October 2025 release is labelled Version 2.1 and the June 2025 release Version 2.1, so version numbers are per-dataset-record and non-monotonic across the series. The record's version_access prose correctly documents this.
'Beta' is taken from the release title '(Beta)'. Supported. The digest gives 'draft, published, deprecated' as examples but does not constrain the slot to an enum, so 'Beta' is acceptable.

The core record carries both `distributions` (ten per-file objects) and `distribution_formats` (three format objects), which overlap substantially: ZIP/application/zip appears in both. If `distributions` is not a declared core slot, this is moot; if it is, the duplication should be reconciled so that per-file detail and format-level description do not restate the same facts.

Internal inconsistency between the two records' handling of the Ravitsky affiliation conflict: both assert `reviewing_organization: The Hastings Center` and both flag the conflict in `source_caveats`, but the full record's dataset-level source_caveats do not mention this conflict while the object-level caveat does, and the core record's dataset-level caveats likewise omit it. A same-tier conflict acknowledged only at object level is easy to miss; it should also surface in the reconciliation report.

Two Maintainer objects both use `role: academic_institution`, but the first describes the CM4AI project consortium and names two individual contacts (Swathi Thaker, Zhandos Sembay) in prose, while the second describes the hosting repository and names the depositor and point of contact in prose. Four named people are carried as free text inside `maintainer_details` where no person-ranged field exists on Maintainer — a structural limitation of the class rather than a record defect, but worth flagging as information at risk of being unqueryable.

30 keywords, all drawn verbatim from the Dataverse keyword list plus the Subject value 'Medicine, Health and Life Sciences'. Including the Subject as a keyword is a mild category blend but harmless and traceable. No unsupported terms introduced.

The Nature publication entry correctly flags that the U2OS map and its data are distinct from the CM4AI cell-line release. This is the right call and is consistently applied — no U2OS-specific facts (275 assemblies, 5,147 proteins, 36,842 interactions, MSV000097168, PXD052362, NDEx uuid, ModelArchive ids) leak into any slot describing this dataset. Verified across the record. Recorded as a positive confirmation of boundary discipline.

Five Instance objects are emitted, one per modality plus one for raw sequence reads. None populates `counts`, which the digest declares as integer. The bundle supplies 11,739 targeted genes for the perturb-seq atlas — a count of perturbations rather than of instances — and no per-modality instance counts for this release (the 53,788 image figure is a project-wide portal aggregate). Omitting `counts` is therefore correct, but the reasoning is not stated in source_caveats.

Four InstanceAcquisition objects correctly separate the three directly-observed modalities from the one derived product (the perturbation cell atlas), with boolean flags set consistently. `was_validated_verified` is left unset throughout; the bundle's Nourreddine reference mentions validation 'via phenotypic, protein-interaction, and metabolic tracing assays' for the atlas, which could support setting it true on the derived-product object.

Both PreprocessingStrategy objects describe the MuSIC pipeline and FAIRSCAPE packaging, and the first carries a source_caveat correctly noting that computed cell maps are not in this release. This means the slot describes processing that produced nothing distributed here. Defensible as context, but it risks implying the distributed archives went through these steps. The FAIRSCAPE packaging (second object) does apply to this release; the MuSIC pipeline (first) largely does not.

summary: Audited both records against the CM4AI bundle and the supplied schema digest. No fabricated dataset facts were found: every substantive claim traces to a bundle source, source-ranking conflicts (IF protein count 464 vs 563 vs 523; project end November 2026 vs 2026-08-31; perturb-seq embargoed vs SRA-linked) are resolved toward the higher tier and disclosed, and the U2OS/Nature dataset is consistently held outside the referent boundary. The most serious issues are structural rather than factual. (1) The core record's `distributions` slot is not present in the supplied schema digest, which declares `file_collections` and `distribution_formats` instead; if the core schema does not define it, ten objects fail validation and the per-file inventory including all MD5 checksums is lost. (2) That same slot causes a paired-record divergence: the core states per-file checksums, paths and media types as structured fields while the full record carries them only as prose inside `file_collections[].description`, so the core asserts structure the full record does not. (3) The 47-author citation is relocated into core `notes` because the core schema lacks `citation`, another silent projection loss. Secondary defects cluster around identifiers and prose-in-description: three Person identifiers use mailto URIs where the bundle supplies ORCIDs in the same release metadata (Ravitsky, Bélisle-Pipon, Parker); three of four Creator objects leave the declared `affiliations` slot empty while restating affiliation in the nested Person description; `credit_roles` is unused throughout; and `collection_timeframes` leaves the declared `start_date` empty while stating 2025-02-27 in prose. Two same-tier conflicts are acknowledged only at object level (Ravitsky's affiliation: University of Montreal in the citation vs a Hastings Center email in the ethics block) where the uniform rule asks that the disagreement be represented rather than one value selected. Supported omissions worth revisiting: `subsets` (the release is explicitly partitioned by cell line and treatment condition), `relationships` (protein-protein interaction edges are a central data product), `confidential_elements` (embargo is stated), and `labeling_strategies` (HPA antibody scoring and four-channel staining are attested). One derived figure — 'approximately 12.6 GB' for the three image archives — is arithmetic over rounded display sizes presented as fact. Clean areas: identifier CURIE discipline (doi: form used consistently, bare DOI in the string-ranged doi slot, fragments minted only on attested anchors), correct omission of all human-subjects slots given the no-human-subjects assertion, and disciplined exclusion of U2OS-specific accessions and counts.
